Subject: Capacity ask — options for committed GPU lanes and onboarding tempo

Hi Mateo / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at CrescentAI is excited about moving toward a committed footprint so we can guarantee inference latency for our customer-facing features. Before we get internal approvals, procurement asked for a compact set of reservation options that show: cluster size, the minimum always-on GPUs, and an onramp timeline (what activation looks like month-by-month).

High-level constraints from our side:
- Target steady-state throughput ~15M tokens/day once warm.
- Latency SLO 95th <= 250ms for chat traffic.
- Want to enable burst capacity for fine-tuning/experiments (short windows).

Can you send a small matrix (3 options) with clear tradeoffs and any warmup credits or pre-warm steps? Attachments (pricing/worksheet) will help speed approvals.

Best,

Subject: Re: Capacity ask — options for committed GPU lanes and onboarding tempo

Lucy — appreciate the clarity. Attached are two files: a condensed worksheet (crescent-reserve-options.xlsx) and a proposal draft (redwood-proposal-v2.pdf). Below is a short matrix we recommend — three lanes that map to cost / latency / risk tradeoffs. I kept the tech notes short so procurement and engineering can both scan quickly.

Option A — Foundational Lane (lowest up-front)- Cluster footprint: 8x A100 equivalent GPUs (shared across models)- Minimum always-on: 4 GPUs (keeps KV cache warm for steady traffic)- Ramp: Month 0: 2 active; Month 1: 4; Month 2: 6; Month 3: 8 (steady)- Warmup credits: 100k token pre-warm included to prime KV caches- Upside: Lowest monthly commitment; good for phased product ramp- Tradeoff: Higher risk of transient throttles under burst; fallback to hosted model variants included

Option B — Performance Lane (balanced)- Cluster footprint: 16x A100 equivalent GPUs- Minimum always-on: 8 GPUs- Ramp: Month 0: 4 active; Month 1: 8; Month 2: 12; Month 3: 16 (steady)- Warmup credits: 300k tokens + 1 scheduled pre-warm window per month- Upside: Meets 95th 250ms SLO for mixed chat loads with margin; supports modest burst without immediate throttling

Option C — Anchored SLA Lane (lowest latency, highest predictability)- Cluster footprint: 32x A100 equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)- Minimum always-on: 16 GPUs- Ramp: Month 0: 8 active; Month 1: 16; Month 2: 24; Month 3: 32 (steady)- Warmup credits: 750k tokens + 2 warmup cycles + on-call pre-warm before major releases- Upside: Strong headroom for peak campaigns and fine-tuning runs; SLA-backed latency targets and faster support SLAs

Operational notes and safeguards:
- Burst windows: All lanes can request burst capacity for 4-hour windows; burst pricing and priority differ by lane.
- Auto-fallback: If dedicated capacity is saturated, traffic is routed to a pinned hosted-compatible model variant to preserve availability (may have higher latency).
- Quantization guidance: For labs/plans where cost is a primary driver we recommend mixed-precision + int8 quantization for evaluation workloads (we can provide a recommended profile).
- Cancellation / stepdown: We included a 60-day stepdown runway in the proposal to allow a staged decommit.

Next steps: If any of these map to Crescent's risk appetite, we can convert the worksheet into a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications that often influence which lane customers pick:

1) Model footprint and KV cache: If Crescent intends to serve multiple large-chat models concurrently, lean toward Option B or C to avoid cross-model cache thrash. We can reserve GPU slices per model in Option B to reduce interference.

2) Sequence length mix: If your median sequence is >1024 tokens, effective throughput per GPU drops ~20-30% — we'll reflect that in the worksheet if you confirm token distribution.

3) Canary & prewarm plan: Recommend a 2-week canary (10% traffic) before each major activation step to validate latency and error budgets. We can automate canary promotion in the Console and schedule pre-warm windows to align with marketing campaigns.

4) Cost controls: Suggest enabling automatic bucket-level throttles at 95th percentile cost thresholds to avoid surprise spend during experiments.

If you want, I can update the worksheet with a per-month token burn estimate tied to your March–May traffic sample.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
